title: Canary-as-Code for Verified Performance Profiles with Autoscale Boundary Annotations
text:
Canary-as-Code for Verified Performance Profiles with Autoscale Boundary Annotations

description:
Implement an automated, declarative canary pipeline (canary-as-code) that publishes Redwood-verified performance profiles together with an 'autoscale-boundary' annotation. The goal is to enable deterministic canaries that validate latency/throughput/cost claims, produce a rollback score if thresholds are violated, and automatically attach autoscale boundary suggestions (min/max GPU pools, batch/latency knobs) to the published profile. This work ties model onboarding, version pinning, and profile publishing so teams can safely publish profiles from CI and have programmatic guardrails for Dedicated/Private deployments.

acceptance_criteria:
A git-backed canary manifest format (.canary.yaml) is defined and documented in Confluence with examples for single-variant and multi-variant models
CI job (github.com/redwood-inference/perf-profiles/actions) runs canary against a stable shadow harness producing signed verification artifacts
Canary results produce a deterministic rollback_score (0-100) and a human-readable failure_reason when rollback_score >= 70
Published profile JSON includes autoscale_boundaries: {min_pool, max_pool, recommended_batch_target, latency_p99_slo} and these fields are surfaced in the Console UI
On publish, profile metadata is annotated with the canary CI run id, sample weights, regional-normalization table, and cost_delta_pct compared to a baseline
Automated rollbacks: if post-publish streaming telemetry (first 24h) shows cost_delta_pct > 15% coupled with latency_regression >= 20ms p99, an automated rollback ticket is opened in Linear and tags responsible owners
E2E tests in the onboarding pipeline simulate failure modes (cold-start KV cache miss, GPU throttling, network egress spike) and assert rollback_score reflects severity

tasks:
Design canary manifest schema and YAML examples
Extend verification runner to emit rollback_score and autoscale boundary heuristics
Add signed verification artifact upload to artifact registry and link into profile publish API
Console: show canary provenance, autoscale boundaries, and rollback rationale in profile detail page
CI: add GitHub Actions workflow 'perf-canary-publish' and required secrets/KMS integration
Create playbook for manual intervention and automated rollback ticketing
Run staged on internal model set (10 models) and collect telemetry for 2 weeks

notes:
This approach moves profile verification left into CI and treats publish as a signed, reversible operation. Autoscale boundary suggestions are heuristic today and will be refined by runtime telemetry. We must coordinate with Dedicated autoscaler and Private deployment upgrade teams before shipping enforcement. Initial rollout will be opt-in for model stewards.

risks:
Autoscale heuristics may recommend overly conservative min_pool leading to unnecessary spend
Rollback_score thresholds need calibration to avoid noisy rollbacks
Publishing from CI increases blast radius if signing keys are compromised

mitigations:
Require two-step signoff for publish for first 6 weeks (CI + steward approval)
Telemetry-based calibration job to tune rollback_score weights after each staged run
Rotate KMS signing keys and limit usage to designated CI runners
